parts.latex:
Michael borrows \$25 000 to purchase a car.  The amount he owes $(A_n)$ on the car after $n$ months can be given by the recursive equation:

$$A_n=A_{n-1}\times 1.015-500$$

Given that $A_0=25\,000$, what amount does Michael owe after 3 months?
What is the domain of $y=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{9-x}}$ ?

A function $f(x)$ is obtained by performing the following operations on $g(x)=\sqrt{x^3+9}$ in the following order:

\begin{enumerate}
\item Reflection in the $y$ axis.
\item Horizontal dilation by a factor of 4.
\item Vertical translation of 1 unit up.
\end{enumerate}

Which of the following is the equation of $f(x)$ ?

The sum of the first ten terms of an arithmetic sequence is $(-50)$.  The next ten terms of this sequence add to $(-450)$.  Find the first term and common difference of the sequence.

solutions.latex:
As the sequence is decreasing by 7 to find the successive term, the sequence is arithmetic with a common difference of $-7$.

Answer: B

$$\begin{aligned}x^2+x-12&=0\\(x-3)(x+4)&=0\\x&=3\text{ or }x=-4\end{aligned}$$

$x^2+x-12>0$ when $x>3$ or $x<-4$

Answer: A

The denominator of a fraction cannot be zero.

$$\begin{aligned}9-x&>0\\x&<9\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Domain is $x\in(-\infty,9)$

Answer: A

$g(x)=\sqrt{x^3+9}$ becomes

$g(-x)=\sqrt{(-x)^3+9}$ after the reflection in the $y$ axis

$$\begin{aligned}g\left(\dfrac{-x}{4}\right)&=\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{-x}{4}\right)^3+9}\quad\text{after a horizontal dilation by a factor of 4}\\&=\sqrt{\dfrac{-x^3}{64}+9}\\&=\sqrt{9-\dfrac{x^3}{64}}\end{aligned}$$

$g\left(\dfrac{-x}{4}\right)+1=\sqrt{9-\dfrac{x^3}{64}}+1$ after a vertical translation of 1 unit

solutions.latex:
Measurements are $0.15,\ 0.153,\ 0.15606$

Geometric sequence where $a=0.15$, $r=1.02$, $T_n=10$

$$\begin{aligned}10&=0.15(1.02)^{n-1}\\\dfrac{200}{3}&=(1.02)^{n-1}\\\ln_{1.02}\left(\dfrac{200}{3}\right)&=n-1\\n-1&=\dfrac{\ln\left(\dfrac{200}{3}\right)}{\ln(1.02)}\\n&=213.078176\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ On the $214^{th}$ day, the salinity will exceed 10 ppt.

Since the series is geometric $\dfrac{T_3}{T_2}=\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}$

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{x}{2x+3}&=\dfrac{2x-3}{x}\\x^2&=(2x-3)(2x+3)\\4x^2-9&=x^2\\3x^2&=9\\x&=\pm\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$$

Even function if $f(x)=f(-x)$

$$\begin{aligned}f(-x)&=\dfrac{8}{(-x)^2+4}\\&=\dfrac{8}{x^2+4}\\&=f(x)\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore f(x)=\dfrac{8}{x^2+4}$ is an even function

Since $x^2>0$, domain is all real $x$

Range: Minimum value of $x^2+4$ is 4 (when $x=0$)

$\therefore$ Maximum value of $y=\dfrac{8}{x^2+4}$ is 2.

As $x\to\pm\infty$, $\dfrac{8}{x^2+4}\to 0$

Range is $0<y\leq 2$
